svg.title: stdx's regular expressions on rebar's curated set against Rust's regex and Go's regexp, on AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor
svg.desc: rebar's curated searches, in multiples of Rust regex's speed: against Rust regex: ahead on 27 (1 inside 5%), level on 0, behind on 4 (1 inside 5%) of 31 rows, 31 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 1.44; from 0.72 to 7.33; against Go regexp: ahead on 30, level on 1, behind on 0 of 31. rebar's curated compiles, in multiples of Rust regex's speed: against Rust regex: ahead on 10, level on 0, behind on 0 of 10 rows, 10 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 5.33; from 3.59 to 10.19; against Go regexp: ahead on 9, level on 0, behind on 1 of 10.
svg.text: stdx's regular expressions on rebar's curated set against Rust's regex and Go's regexp, on AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor
The median of 5 jobs on AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor, the CPU model of 5 of 18 jobs, the most of any: runs
The bars share one logarithmic axis of stdx over Rust regex. The other libraries stand in the columns at the right.
A bar is the median of stdx over Rust regex:
|—| the interval of the median: the jobs' lowest to highest ratio, 94% confidence
the median of another CPU model's jobs: AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor (3), AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor (4),
rebar's curated searches, in multiples of Rust regex's speed
against Rust regex: ahead on 27 (1 inside 5%), level on 0, behind on 4 (1 inside 5%) of 31 rows, 31 patterns; geometric mean over these
against Go regexp: ahead on 30, level on 1, behind on 0 of 31
Each row is a benchmark of rebar's curated set whose engines name Go's regexp or RE2, under rebar's own model, pattern and haystack.
rebar's author chose them, and design §8 part 22n tuned stdx on them since, so they no longer show how stdx runs on patterns its tuning
did not see. rebar's author also wrote Rust's crate, and rebar's BIAS.md says the set may favor that crate.
rebar's curated compiles, in multiples of Rust regex's speed
against Rust regex: ahead on 10, level on 0, behind on 0 of 10 rows, 10 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 5.33; from 3.59 to 10.19
against Go regexp: ahead on 9, level on 0, behind on 1 of 10
A row is ahead or behind where its interval lies above or below 1, and level where it holds 1 inside 5% of 1. A row whose interval holds 1
and reaches past 5% is unclear: its jobs do not settle it. A difference inside 5% is one this chart calls too small to matter, and the
counts still name its direction. A bar ahead or behind inside 5% is drawn lighter, and the shaded band on each panel is 5% of 1.
The columns at the right are stdx's speed over another library's, the median of the jobs. A library has no speed (—) on a pattern that it
refuses, where its answer is not Go regexp's, and where it has no such call.
stdx timed again, last in each round, differed from stdx by at most 6.4% in any job of any row.
On another CPU model, these rows fall on the other side of 1: 02-literal-alternate/sherlock-casei-en (INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C,
